age.evidence: For head-twitch response and learned helplessness, 6 to 10-week-old C57BL/6J mice were used. For electrophysiology, 6 to 8-week-old C57BL/6J mice were used. For two-photon imaging, Thy1 GFP mice underwent surgery when they were 6 to 8-week-old... For confocal imaging, 8 to 12-week-old Thy1 GFP mice were used.

sex.evidence: Head-twitch response was evaluated using 40 male and 42 female C57BL/6J mice. Learned helplessness was evaluated using 34 male and 34 female C57BL/6J mice.

dosing.evidence: Animals were weighed and injected intraperitoneally with saline or psilocybin (0.25, 0.5, 1, or 2 mg/kg).
For ketanserin pretreated groups, animals received ketanserin (1 mg/kg, i.p.; S006, Sigma-Aldrich) 10 min before administration of saline or psilocybin (1 mg/kg, i.p.).
injected with saline (10 mL/kg, i.p.), ketamine (10 mg/kg, i.p.), or psilocybin (1 mg/kg, i.p.)

handling.evidence: Upon arrival, animals habituated at the housing facility for > 2 weeks before behavioral testing. (No explicit handling protocol described.)

group_housing.evidence: Mice were group housed (2 - 5 mice per cage) under controlled temperature in a 12 hr light-dark cycle (7:00 AM to 7:00 PM) with free access to food and water.

day_night_flipped.evidence: 12 hr light-dark cycle (7:00 AM to 7:00 PM)

assays.assay_description: Mice individually placed in halved open-field activity boxes immediately after i.p. injection of psilocybin (0.25–2 mg/kg) with or without ketanserin pretreatment; head twitches counted from overhead video. Typical recordings 30 min; subset extended to >150 min.

application_type.evidence: injected intraperitoneally with saline or psilocybin (0.25, 0.5, 1, or 2 mg/kg).

setup_habituation.evidence: No pre-test exposure to the apparatus described.

setup_restrain.evidence: the two animals were immediately placed into separate chambers, made by inserting a plastic divider to halve an open-field-activity box

food_restriction.evidence: Testing in an open-field activity box; no food in apparatus during recording.

water_restriction.evidence: Testing in an open-field activity box; no water in apparatus during recording.

time_to_assay.evidence: after injections, the two animals were immediately placed into separate chambers

sample_size.evidence: We characterized 82 C57BL/6J mice (40 males and 42 females) with five doses of psilocybin (0, 0.25, 0.5, 1, and 2 mg/kg, intraperitoneally [i.p.]; range, 7-10 per sex per dose).

outcomes.summary: Psilocybin produced a dose-dependent increase in head-twitch response with a sharp rise at 1 mg/kg; the response peaked at 6-8 min post-administration and declined to zero by ~2 h. Ketanserin (1 mg/kg) pretreatment fully abolished the head-twitch response.
outcomes.statistics: A Kruskal-Wallis test was used to compare 10-minute head twitch responses across treatment groups (Saline+Psilocybin vs Ketanserin+Psilocybin vs Ketanserin+Saline), followed by Dunn's multiple comparisons.
outcomes.evidence: A sharp rise of elicited head-twitch responses occurred at 1 mg/kg... rate of head-twitch responses peaked at 6-8 min after administration and then gradually declined until they ceased at ~2h. The ketanserin pretreatment abolished completely the psilocybin-induced head-twitch responses.

B1_num_measures.evidence: The videos were scored for head twitches.

B2_temporal_dynamics.evidence: Time course of head-twitch responses after administrating psilocybin... peaked at 6-8 min after administration and then gradually declined

B4_ethological.evidence: HTR is a pharmacological reflex, explicitly excluded from ethological behaviours by rubric.

B5_social.evidence: the two animals were immediately placed into separate chambers

B7_automated_classification.evidence: The videos were scored for head twitches by an experienced observer blind to the experimental conditions.

E1_environment_type.evidence: open-field-activity box (12'' W x 6'' H x 10'' D)

E3_bedding.evidence: Bare open-field box, cleaned with 70% ethanol between mice.

E6_spatial.evidence: plastic divider halved an open-field-activity box; each animal in a single open compartment

E7_social_context.evidence: the two animals were immediately placed into separate chambers

D1_continuity.evidence: Typical recordings were 30 minutes long and, for a subset of mice (2 males and 2 females), extended to > 150 minutes.

D2_session_duration.evidence: for a subset of mice (2 males and 2 females), extended to > 150 minutes

D4_baseline.evidence: Recording began after drug administration; no pre-drug baseline.

assays.assay_description: 5-day protocol in a two-compartment shuttle box. Days 1-2: inescapable footshocks (induction). Day 3 (Test 1): 30 escapable footshocks (0.15 mA, ≤10 s) measuring escape failures and latency. Day 4: i.p. saline, ketamine (10 mg/kg) or psilocybin (1 mg/kg). Day 5 (Test 2, 24 h after treatment): identical test.

application_type.evidence: injected with saline (10 mL/kg, i.p.), ketamine (10 mg/kg, i.p.), or psilocybin (1 mg/kg, i.p.)

setup_restrain.evidence: allowed the animal to shuttle between two compartments

food_restriction.evidence: Shuttle box test; no food in apparatus during recording.

water_restriction.evidence: Shuttle box test; no water in apparatus during recording.

time_to_assay.evidence: On Day 5, 24 hr after treatment, the animal underwent Test 2

sample_size.evidence: Learned helplessness was evaluated using 34 male and 34 female C57BL/6J mice... We used 68 C57BL/6J mice to compare psilocybin (1 mg/kg, i.p.) against saline and ketamine (10 mg/kg, i.p.).

outcomes.summary: Within individuals, psilocybin (1 mg/kg) reduced escape failures from Test 1 to Test 2 (24 h post-dose); in susceptible animals 15 of 16 psilocybin-treated mice showed a decrease or no change. Across groups, comparison of saline vs ketamine vs psilocybin did not reach a main effect of treatment.
outcomes.statistics: p = 0.004, post hoc Bonferroni-corrected t test (within-individual); p = 0.09, two-way ANOVA (across treatments).
outcomes.evidence: Within individuals, psilocybin reduced the proportion of escape failures (p = 0.004, post hoc Bonferroni-corrected t test; Figure 1D)... Across individuals, comparison among saline, ketamine, and psilocybin did not reveal a main effect of treatment (p = 0.09, two-way ANOVA; Figure 1E).

B1_num_measures.evidence: Escape failures and escape latencies were used as indicators of learned helplessness

B5_social.evidence: An animal was placed in a shuttle box

B6_cognitive.evidence: Learned helplessness paradigm requires learning escape contingencies.

E1_environment_type.evidence: shuttle box separated by a guillotine door (16'' x 6.5'' x 8.5'', Med Associates Inc.)

E2_shelter.evidence: Two open compartments, no enclosed refuge.

E6_spatial.evidence: shuttle box separated by a guillotine door which, when open, allowed the animal to shuttle between two compartments

E7_social_context.evidence: An animal was placed in a shuttle box

D1_continuity.evidence: On Day 3, the animal underwent Test 1... On Day 5, 24 hr after treatment, the animal underwent Test 2.

D2_session_duration.evidence: 30 footshocks with up to 10 s each followed by 30 s inter-shock interval ≈ ~20 min per test session.

D3_recording_days.evidence: Test 1 on Day 3 and Test 2 on Day 5.

D4_baseline.evidence: Test 1 served as a pre-drug baseline before treatment on Day 4.

D5_followup.evidence: On Day 5, 24 hr after treatment, the animal underwent Test 2.

judge_notes: Only two behavioural assays were administered to rodents with a psychedelic: head-twitch response and learned helplessness. Two-photon/confocal imaging, whole-cell mEPSC recording are non-behavioural endpoints and were excluded per rubric.
Added Ketanserin and Ketamine to dosing block (only qwen/glm omitted them); they were administered to behavioural-test animals.
HTR D2 set to score 2 (61 min–6 h) because a subset of mice was recorded >150 min — the longest session sets the score.
Learned helplessness D2 set to 15–60 min based on protocol arithmetic (30 trials × up to 10 s shock + 30 s ITI ≈ 20 min); confidence medium since paper does not state a total session duration.
B2 for learned helplessness scored 0: paper does not analyse within-session time course of escape behaviour.
E2 for shuttle box scored 0: open compartments are not enclosed refuges (glm's score of 1 overridden).
Outcomes time_dependent for learned helplessness set to n/a (single post-dose timepoint) rather than 'yes'.
